sentences.text: There is only one known species, Anchiornis huxleyi, a small, bipedal theropod roughly the size of a crow. This animal possessed a triangular skull sharing traits with dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and primitive avialans. While its body was covered in feathers, it also retained scales on specific body parts.

The genus Anchiornis was described by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2009. The type specimen, held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology with catalogue number IVPP V14378, was discovered in the Yaolugou area of Jianchang County, Liaoning, China.

The hind leg feathers likely served a display function rather than flight, as they lacked the shape and arrangement of true flight feathers. Anchiornis displayed complex coloration with speckled patterns across its body and wings, likely used for communication or display. Its forelimbs measured 80% of the total length of its hindlimbs. A 2016 study suggested juvenile Anchiornis might have used wings to assist running up inclines, though adults likely could not gain aerodynamic benefits from flapping.

Avialans are more closely related to modern birds than to dromaeosaurid and troodontid dinosaurs. A 2017 re-evaluation placed Anchiornis in the family Anchiornithidae alongside genera like Eosinopteryx and Xiaotingia. The Paleobiology Database lists Troodontidae as the parent group for Anchiornis.

Anchiornis fossils date to the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) period, living about 160 million years ago. Most studies date the rocks containing these fossils to between 160.89 and 160.25 million years ago.

The status of Aurornis xui, Eosinopteryx brevipenna, and Serikornis sungei as synonyms of Anchiornis is questioned. A 2015 study of a second Anchiornis fossil found only gray-black melanosomes, contradicting the 2010 findings of rufous coloration. Researchers hypothesized that the rufous color might have been replaced as the smaller Beijing Museum specimen aged. It is debated whether regional differences or distinct species of Anchiornis caused the variation in plumage color patterns.
